chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from his father, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said:
I asked ʿAli ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And were it not that the people would become one community.

He (عليه السلام) said: What is meant by that is the community of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), that if they were to be upon one religion as disbelievers, all of them, We would surely have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses.

And if Allah had done that with the community of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), the believers would have grieved, and that would have saddened them; and they would not have married them, nor inherited from them.

key_terms.أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً: a single community united upon one way
key_terms.أُمَّةَ مُحَمَّدٍ: the community of Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.بِالرَّحْمٰنِ: in the Most Merciful, referring to Allah
key_terms.دِينٍ وَاحِدٍ: one religion or one shared religious path

ai.seo_question: What does the verse 'And were it not that the people would become one community' mean according to Imam ʿAli ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This narration explains the verse as referring to the Ummah of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), stating that if all people had united upon disbelief, Allah could have granted great worldly luxury to the disbelievers. The narration highlights that such visible favor toward disbelievers would have deeply distressed the believers and affected social relations such as marriage and inheritance.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Ghalib, from his father, from Saeed Bin Al Musayyab who said,
‘I asked Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[43:33] And were it not that all people had been a single nation.

Heasws said: ‘It Means by that the community of Muhammadsaww, if they had happened to be upon one Religion, they would have been disbeliever, all of them We would certainly have Assigned to those who disbelieve in the Beneficent (to make) of silver the roofs of their houses.
And had Allahazwj Done that with the community of Muhammadsaww, the Momineen would have grieved and that would have saddened them, and would not have married them and would not have inherited them’.
en.sarwar: 23. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ghalib from his father from Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib who has said the following:
“Once I asked Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘Were it not that all people would become one nation, . . .’

- and the Imam said, ‘It (all people) stands for the followers of Muhammad (a.s.) all of whom might turn to disbelief, - ‘ ... We would have made for the unbelievers in the Beneficent, ceilings out of silver. . . [43:33]

Had Allah done so to the followers of Muhammad (a.s.) the believers might feel very depressed and they would not establish any marital relations with and inheritance for those turning to disbelief (thus, they might become extinct).’”

Note: To understand better, read the whole verse: ‘Were it not that all people would become one nation, We would have made for the unbelievers in the Beneficent, ceilings out of silver. . . (43:33 Had all unbelievers been given so much wealth, the common Muslims might have abandoned their religion considering the prosperity of the unbelievers as a sign of Allah’s happiness with them. In fact, according to Allah, worldly things are of no significance at all.
